# Selector Drift Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** A scheduled extraction pipeline that re-resolves page elements when a UI changes, proves each heal correct through an unskippable validation gate, and refuses to write when it cannot.

**Architecture:** A type-gated spine. Each stage returns a type the next stage structurally requires, so the two safety gates cannot be bypassed by forgetting to call them. `scope/` is the only module that can mint an `AuthorisedTarget`; `validate/` is the only module that can mint a `ValidatedExtraction`; `land.write()` accepts nothing else. A five-rung resolution cascade heals broken selectors, and a six-check gate judges every heal — including a cross-family re-resolution that catches the adjacent-column failure with no history needed.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3.12+, `uv`, `ruff`, `mypy --strict`, `import-linter`, Pydantic v2, Playwright (containerised, pinned), Prefect 3, Postgres + Alembic, Parquet + DuckDB, FastAPI, Next.js 15 + `bok-ui` (minimal slice, absolute `file:` path until published), `bok-core` (minimal slice, absolute editable path until published), test bench on FastAPI + Jinja2 + `lxml`, pytest + hypothesis, axe-core.

**Spec:** [`docs/superpowers/specs/2024-11-07-selector-drift-design.md`](../specs/2024-11-07-selector-drift-design.md), plus four sub-specs added 2026-09-26 that the rewritten tasks implement: [API contract and evidence bundle](../specs/2026-09-26-selector-drift-api-contract.md) · [web UI](../specs/2026-09-26-selector-drift-web-ui.md) · [test-bench portal](../specs/2026-09-26-selector-drift-testbench-portal.md) · [`bok-ui` slice](../specs/2026-09-26-selector-drift-bok-ui-slice.md). Executors read the design and the sub-spec named in their task.
**Audit:** [`docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-08-29-plan-audit.md`](../reviews/2026-08-29-plan-audit.md) — 63 findings; revisions R1–R17 are applied below and each carries its finding id. The 2026-09-26 revision is logged at the end.

## Global Constraints

- Python 3.12+, `uv` for dependencies, `ruff` for lint+format, `mypy --strict` on every module. TypeScript strict mode, no `any` without a justifying comment.
- Licence **Apache-2.0**. Repo **private until first release (build week 8)**, per the programme decision — flipping a repo public preserves its full git history, so the ninety-day log's start date stays verifiable. The nightly cron runs on the P-4 VM, not on Actions, so the Actions allowance constrains CI only.
- **$0 recurring cost.** No dependency with a paid floor.
- **No secrets in the repo, ever, including fixtures.** `gitleaks` pre-commit + CI.
- **Zero model calls in v1.** No `bok_core.gateway` import anywhere. Rung 5 escalates; it does not call a model.
- **No `[project.scripts]`, no Typer/Click.** Dev entrypoint is `python -m selector_drift`. Buyer entrypoint is the Prefect scheduler.
- **No TOTP seed storage.** No field named or typed for a TOTP seed exists anywhere in the schema. Enforced by a test (Task 31).
- **No write-back into a client portal.** `land/` writes to our lake only; the change-set export (Task 30) produces a file the client applies.
- Scope bases in v1 are exactly `self-owned` and `client-authorised`. `public-permissive` is refused.
- Everything runs from `docker compose up` with only `.env.example` copied.
- Coverage floor 75%. axe zero serious/critical.
- Every subprocess containerised: non-root, read-only rootfs, tmpfs scratch, **seccomp default — never `unconfined`**, `cap_drop: [ALL]`, `no-new-privileges`, memory and pid limits, hard timeout. (R8/H1)
- **No `eval`, no `exec`, no `yaml.load`.** Every YAML loader is `yaml.safe_load`; every spec-supplied expression goes through the restricted evaluator from Task 21. A task spec is config, and config must never be code. (R13/H5)
- **The browser never leaves the authorised origin.** Every request is checked against an allowlist derived from the `AuthorisedTarget`; anything else is aborted. (R8/H2)
- **The API authenticates, and `actor` is never taken from a request body.** (R16/H3)
- **Every model of the world that a published number depends on is a table, not a log line.** `resolutions`, `run_attempts`, `deploys` and `heartbeats` ship on day one with the rest of the frozen schema. (R5/C4; `heartbeats` added 2026-09-26)
- **`bok_core` imports are allow-listed, not deny-listed.** `tests/test_bok_core_allowlist.py` (Task 1) AST-walks `selector_drift/` and fails on any `bok_core` import outside `ALLOWED`; adding a submodule is one line. Stronger than naming `gateway`, which import-linter cannot express for an external package. (Task 1 ledger, 2026-09-26)
- **Every computed figure comes from `selector_drift/api/derive.py`** — the operator UI and the published heal log import the same function, so they cannot disagree. (Task 34B)
- **The test bench ships no JavaScript of its own**, and *served equals tested* is asserted on the browser DOM, never the HTTP body. (bench spec §1)
- **Evidence is never rendered as markup.** Stored DOM is a third party's page: the API serves it sandboxed and `nosniff`, and the UI shows it as escaped text. (API spec §4.2)

**Standing verification commands.** Split by tier so the gate after each task stays under a minute
and therefore actually gets run (M26). `pytest.ini` registers the markers; every test carries exactly
one.

```bash
# the fast check — after every task. No browser, no Postgres, no network.
uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .
uv run mypy --strict selector_drift
uv run lint-imports
uv run pytest -q -m unit -n auto --cov=selector_drift --cov-fail-under=75

# the full check — at each phase boundary and before any commit that closes a task
uv run pytest -q -m "unit or integration" -n auto --cov=selector_drift --cov-fail-under=75
cd web && npx playwright test          # e2e, browser-backed
```

| Marker | May touch | Runtime budget |
|---|---|---|
| `unit` | nothing external. Rungs run against a `StaticPageSource` (Task 13) — **no browser** | < 60 s whole tier |
| `integration` | Postgres, the lake, a local bench fixture | < 5 min |
| `e2e` | a real browser and a served UI | unbounded, CI only |

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the import contracts**

Create `.importlinter`:

```ini
[importlinter]
root_packages = selector_drift, testbench
# REQUIRED (M21). Without it the bok_core.gateway contract names a module outside the graph,
# matches nothing, and reports "kept" — a green tick with no test behind it.
include_external_packages = True

[importlinter:contract:resolver-cannot-write]
name = A resolver cannot write
type = forbidden
source_modules = selector_drift.resolve
forbidden_modules = selector_drift.land

[importlinter:contract:judged-cannot-call-judge]
name = The judged cannot call the judge
type = forbidden
source_modules = selector_drift.resolve
forbidden_modules = selector_drift.validate

[importlinter:contract:heallog-cannot-refetch]
name = Replay uses stored evidence, never a live page
type = forbidden
source_modules = selector_drift.heallog
forbidden_modules = selector_drift.browser
# NB (C6): forbidden contracts report INDIRECT imports by default. Task 19's replay imports
# resolve.cascade, so this contract only holds because Task 13 moves PageSource out of browser/
# into resolve/page.py. Do not add allow_indirect_imports to make this pass — that would be
# suppressing the finding rather than fixing it.

[importlinter:contract:judge-reaches-rungs-only-by-protocol]
name = validate/ may reach rungs only via the public Rung protocol
type = forbidden
source_modules = selector_drift.validate
forbidden_modules = selector_drift.resolve.rungs
# Design 3.4 claims this contract; without this stanza it was never implemented (M22).
# Concrete rungs are constructed in orchestrate/ and injected; validate/ sees only Rung + Family.

[importlinter:contract:answer-key-isolation]
name = The resolver cannot see the answer key
type = forbidden
source_modules = selector_drift
forbidden_modules = testbench.answers

# NO no-model-calls stanza here -- see "Replaced 2026-09-26" below. It is enforced by
# tests/test_bok_core_allowlist.py instead.
```

**Replaced 2026-09-26 (Task 1 ledger).** The first text of this contract was
`forbidden_modules = bok_core.gateway`, and import-linter cannot express it on any version:
import-linter 2.14 refuses a subpackage of an external package as a forbidden module, and with
`include_external_packages` every import of an external package is recorded against its **top-level
node**, so the graph cannot tell `bok_core.gateway` from `bok_core.provenance`. For the same reason an
`ignore_imports` allow-list naming `bok_core.provenance.**` cannot be relied on to match anything. The
worktree currently has the stanza commented out and deferred.

The replacement does not depend on import-linter at all. It is an AST walk, and it is **strictly
stronger** than the original — it rejects `gateway` and every other `bok_core` submodule not named:

```python
# tests/test_bok_core_allowlist.py
import ast
from pathlib import Path
import pytest

# One line per submodule a task legitimately needs. Task 29 adds "bok_core.findings";
# Task 33 adds "bok_core.boundary.redact" and "bok_core.boundary.egress".
ALLOWED = {"bok_core.boundary.sensitivity", "bok_core.provenance"}

def _imports(path: Path) -> set[str]:
    tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    found: set[str] = set()
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
            found |= {a.name for a in node.names}
        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module and node.level == 0:
            found.add(node.module)
    return {m for m in found if m == "bok_core" or m.startswith("bok_core.")}

@pytest.mark.unit
def test_selector_drift_imports_only_allow_listed_bok_core_modules() -> None:
    offenders = {
        f"{p}: {m}"
        for p in Path("selector_drift").rglob("*.py")
        for m in _imports(p)
        if not any(m == a or m.startswith(a + ".") for a in ALLOWED)
    }
    assert not offenders, f"bok_core import outside the allow-list (v1 makes zero model calls): {offenders}"
```

Two further deviations from Steps 1–2 below were ruled on in the same ledger: the repo was
hand-scaffolded rather than produced by `copier` (P-2), and `bok-core` is an absolute-path editable
dependency rather than a PyPI install (P-1). `root_packages` must be written one per line: 2.14 splits
list values on newlines, never on commas.

### Task 2: The scope gate — build the refusal before the crawler

**Files:**
- Create: `selector_drift/scope/record.py`, `selector_drift/scope/gate.py`, `selector_drift/scope/errors.py`, `selector_drift/scope/_token.py`
- Test: `tests/scope/test_gate.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: nothing.
- Produces:
  - `ScopeRecord` (Pydantic v2) with fields `target: str`, `basis: Basis`, `authorising_party: str`, `authorised_on: date`, `expires_on: date`, `evidence_uri: str | None`, `evidence_sha256: str | None`, `origins: list[str]`, `rate_limit: RateLimit`, `user_agent_contact: str`, `first_heal_policy: FirstHealPolicy`, `legal_review: str`
  - **`sensitivity` is not an author-writable field (R4/H7).** It is a derived property:
    `SELF_OWNED -> SYNTHETIC`, `CLIENT_AUTHORISED -> CLIENT_CONFIDENTIAL`. A free-text label that
    gates publication means one typo in one YAML file publishes a client's portal screenshots — the
    exact outcome B4 exists to prevent, reachable with no second control. Derived, it cannot be typed
    wrong.
  - `origins: list[str]` — the only origins this target may reach. Consumed by Task 4's allowlist (H2)
  - `evidence_sha256` — **required whenever `evidence_uri` is set (R3/H10).** The scope record is the
    document you point at if anyone asks why you accessed a system; "trust the working tree" is not
    integrity. `authorise()` re-hashes the referenced file and refuses on mismatch
  - `Basis` — `StrEnum` with exactly `SELF_OWNED = "self-owned"` and `CLIENT_AUTHORISED = "client-authorised"`
  - `FirstHealPolicy` — `StrEnum` with `REQUIRED = "required"`, `AUTO_PROMOTE = "auto_promote"`
  - `RateLimit(requests: int, per_seconds: int)`
  - `AuthorisedTarget` — frozen dataclass; constructor requires the **singleton** `_MINT` token from
    `scope/_token.py`, and `__post_init__` asserts *identity*, not merely type (M29). A leading
    underscore is a convention, not a control: `from ... import _ScopeToken` works. The real
    enforcement is the identity check plus an import-linter contract on the token module — add to
    `.importlinter`:

    ```ini
    [importlinter:contract:only-the-gate-mints]
    name = Only scope.gate may reach the mint token
    type = forbidden
    source_modules =
        selector_drift.browser
        selector_drift.resolve
        selector_drift.validate
        selector_drift.extract
        selector_drift.land
        selector_drift.orchestrate
        selector_drift.heallog
        selector_drift.api
    forbidden_modules = selector_drift.scope._token
    ```
  - `authorise(record: ScopeRecord, *, today: date) -> AuthorisedTarget` — raises `ScopeRefusal`
  - `ScopeRefusal(Exception)` with `.reason: str`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**

```python
# tests/scope/test_gate.py
import datetime as dt
import pytest
from selector_drift.scope.record import ScopeRecord, Basis, AuthorisedTarget
from selector_drift.scope.gate import authorise
from selector_drift.scope.errors import ScopeRefusal

TODAY = dt.date(2026, 9, 7)

def rec(**kw):
    base = dict(
        target="testbench", basis=Basis.SELF_OWNED, authorising_party="me",
        authorised_on=dt.date(2026, 9, 1), expires_on=dt.date(2027, 9, 1),
        evidence_uri=None, evidence_sha256=None,
        origins=["https://bench.example.invalid"],
        rate_limit={"requests": 1, "per_seconds": 30},
        user_agent_contact="https://example.invalid/contact",
        first_heal_policy="required", legal_review="self_drafted",
    )
    return ScopeRecord(**(base | kw))

def test_valid_self_owned_record_is_authorised():
    assert authorise(rec(), today=TODAY).target == "testbench"

def test_expired_authorisation_is_refused():
    with pytest.raises(ScopeRefusal, match="expired"):
        authorise(rec(expires_on=dt.date(2026, 9, 6)), today=TODAY)

def test_public_permissive_basis_does_not_exist():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        rec(basis="public-permissive")

def test_client_authorised_without_evidence_is_refused():
    with pytest.raises(ScopeRefusal, match="evidence_uri"):
        authorise(rec(basis=Basis.CLIENT_AUTHORISED, evidence_uri=None), today=TODAY)

def test_authorised_target_cannot_be_built_outside_the_gate():
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        AuthorisedTarget(target="anything", basis=Basis.SELF_OWNED)  # type: ignore[call-arg]

def test_a_forged_token_is_rejected_by_identity_not_by_type():
    """M29. A leading underscore is a convention. Someone WILL import _ScopeToken --
    probably a test fixture at 2am. Type-checking the token catches nothing; only
    identity against the singleton minted in gate.py does."""
    from selector_drift.scope._token import _ScopeToken
    with pytest.raises(ScopeRefusal, match="mint"):
        AuthorisedTarget(_ScopeToken(), target="anything", basis=Basis.SELF_OWNED,
                         rate_limit=RateLimit(1, 30), origins=[], user_agent_contact="",
                         first_heal_policy="required", sensitivity="SYNTHETIC",
                         expires_on=dt.date(2027, 1, 1))

def test_sensitivity_is_derived_from_basis_and_cannot_be_authored():
    """R4/H7. SYNTHETIC skips the redaction argument and permits publication.
    If it is a field, one typo publishes a client portal."""
    assert "sensitivity" not in ScopeRecord.model_fields
    assert rec(basis=Basis.SELF_OWNED).sensitivity == "SYNTHETIC"
    assert rec(basis=Basis.CLIENT_AUTHORISED, evidence_uri="file://a",
               evidence_sha256="0" * 64).sensitivity == "CLIENT_CONFIDENTIAL"

def test_client_authorised_evidence_must_hash_to_what_the_record_claims(tmp_path):
    """R3/H10."""
    doc = tmp_path / "authorisation.pdf"; doc.write_bytes(b"countersigned")
    with pytest.raises(ScopeRefusal, match="evidence_sha256"):
        authorise(rec(basis=Basis.CLIENT_AUTHORISED, evidence_uri=doc.as_uri(),
                      evidence_sha256="0" * 64), today=TODAY)

def test_a_record_with_no_origins_is_refused():
    """H2. An empty allowlist means the browser may go anywhere, which is the
    opposite of what a scope record is for."""
    with pytest.raises(ScopeRefusal, match="origins"):
        authorise(rec(origins=[]), today=TODAY)

def test_authorised_on_after_expires_on_is_refused():
    with pytest.raises(ScopeRefusal):
        authorise(rec(authorised_on=dt.date(2027, 1, 1),
                      expires_on=dt.date(2026, 12, 1)), today=TODAY)

def test_expiry_is_evaluated_in_utc_never_local_time():
    """M20. The run window, the mutation seed and this check must agree on a
    calendar or the bench's answer key drifts by a day at the boundary."""
    import selector_drift.scope.gate as g
    assert "date.today()" not in inspect.getsource(g)
```

**`today` is always passed in, never defaulted, and every caller passes
`datetime.now(UTC).date()`** (M20). Note also that the fixtures above use a fixed `TODAY` rather than
`dt.date.today()`: a test that compares a wall clock to a hardcoded `expires_on` is green until that
date and red afterwards for no reason anyone will remember.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement the record and the token-gated mint site**

`_token.py` holds the mint control and nothing else, so the import-linter contract above has
something to point at:

```python
class _ScopeToken:
    __slots__ = ()

_MINT = _ScopeToken()      # the only instance the gate will accept
```

`record.py` defines the enums, `ScopeRecord`, the derived `sensitivity` property, and:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AuthorisedTarget:
    _token: _ScopeToken
    target: str
    basis: Basis
    rate_limit: RateLimit
    origins: tuple[str, ...]          # H2 -- the browser allowlist
    user_agent_contact: str
    first_heal_policy: FirstHealPolicy
    sensitivity: Sensitivity          # derived from basis, never authored
    expires_on: date
    record_sha256: str                # H10 -- what this run will write to audit_log

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self._token is not _MINT:              # identity, not isinstance (M29)
            raise ScopeRefusal("not minted by the scope gate")
```

`gate.py` implements `authorise()`, refusing on each of, in order:

| Refusal | Audit |
|---|---|
| `expires_on < today` | brief §3.1 |
| `authorised_on > expires_on` | — |
| `basis` outside the v1 enum | design §4.2 |
| `basis is CLIENT_AUTHORISED and evidence_uri is None` | design §4.2 |
| `evidence_uri` set and its bytes do not hash to `evidence_sha256` | R3/H10 |
| `origins` empty | R8/H2 |
| `rate_limit.requests < 1 or per_seconds < 1` | H4 |

On success it returns `AuthorisedTarget(_MINT, ..., record_sha256=sha256(yaml_bytes))`. Every run
writes that hash to `audit_log`, so "which authorisation was in force when we accessed this system"
is answerable from the database rather than from the working tree.

#### ScopeRecord additions for Task 2

**Two fields join `ScopeRecord`, both for the same reason as `first_heal_policy`: a value that a
client target must never quietly lower lives on the scope record, next to the authorisation basis.**

- `warmup_runs: int` — `Field(default=30, ge=1)`. The bench's record sets `5` (design §5.7, M18);
  client targets keep the default `30`. `ge=1` because `0` means "trust a heal with no history",
  which is the thing warm-up exists to prevent.
- `evidence_retention_days: int | None` — `Field(default=None, ge=1)`. `None` means "kept for the
  life of the log" and is **permitted only for `self-owned`**. For `client-authorised` a missing
  value is a **refusal at `authorise()`, not a default** (API spec §7.4, closes M30): an unbounded
  retention of client screenshots is exactly what `00` B7 exists to prevent, and a default would be
  the gate silently choosing a retention policy on a client's behalf.

`AuthorisedTarget` gains the same two fields, **as its last two fields with defaults**
(`warmup_runs: int = 30`, `evidence_retention_days: int | None = None`) so that
`test_a_forged_token_is_rejected_by_identity_not_by_type` still reaches the identity check rather
than failing on a missing argument. `authorise()` always passes both explicitly.

The refusal table in Step 3 gains one row, **after** the `evidence_sha256` row and **before** the
`origins` row (so the existing `evidence_uri` and `evidence_sha256` tests still match first):

| Refusal | Audit |
|---|---|
| `basis is CLIENT_AUTHORISED and evidence_retention_days is None` — reason `"evidence_retention_days is required for a client-authorised target"` | API spec §7.4, M30 |

Implementation, in `gate.py` at that position:

```python
    if record.basis is Basis.CLIENT_AUTHORISED and record.evidence_retention_days is None:
        raise ScopeRefusal("evidence_retention_days is required for a client-authorised target")
```

and the mint call gains `warmup_runs=record.warmup_runs,
evidence_retention_days=record.evidence_retention_days`.

Add to `tests/scope/test_gate.py` (the `rec()` helper is unchanged — both new fields have defaults):

```python
import hashlib
from pydantic import ValidationError


def _client_rec(tmp_path, **kw):
    doc = tmp_path / "authorisation.pdf"
    doc.write_bytes(b"countersigned")
    return rec(basis=Basis.CLIENT_AUTHORISED, evidence_uri=doc.as_uri(),
               evidence_sha256=hashlib.sha256(b"countersigned").hexdigest(), **kw)


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_client_target_without_retention_days_is_refused(tmp_path):
    """API spec 7.4 / M30. A refusal, not a default."""
    with pytest.raises(ScopeRefusal, match="evidence_retention_days"):
        authorise(_client_rec(tmp_path), today=TODAY)


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_client_target_with_retention_days_is_authorised(tmp_path):
    t = authorise(_client_rec(tmp_path, evidence_retention_days=90), today=TODAY)
    assert t.evidence_retention_days == 90


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_self_owned_target_may_keep_evidence_for_the_life_of_the_log():
    assert authorise(rec(), today=TODAY).evidence_retention_days is None


@pytest.mark.unit
@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", [0, -1])
def test_warmup_runs_must_be_at_least_one(bad):
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        rec(warmup_runs=bad)


@pytest.mark.unit
@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", [0, -30])
def test_retention_days_must_be_positive_when_set(bad):
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        rec(evidence_retention_days=bad)


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_warmup_defaults_to_thirty_and_reaches_the_authorised_target():
    assert rec().warmup_runs == 30
    assert authorise(rec(warmup_runs=5), today=TODAY).warmup_runs == 5
```

### Task 3: The full run and heal-event schema — day one, most columns null

**Files:**
- Create: `selector_drift/db/models.py`, `selector_drift/db/session.py`, `alembic/versions/0001_initial.py`
- Test: `tests/db/test_schema.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `Sensitivity`, `Basis` from Task 2.
- Produces: tables `runs`, `heal_events`, `selector_cache`, `quarantine`, `audit_log`, `scope_records`. Later tasks write to these; **none of them may add a column afterwards**, because you cannot compare day 1 to day 90 across a schema migration. This is the one place the plan deliberately builds ahead of need.

Column list, fixed now:

| Table | Columns |
|---|---|
| `runs` | `run_key` (PK, `f"{target}:{spec_version}:{window}"`), `target`, `spec_version`, `window`, `first_started_at`, `last_finished_at`, `state` (`completed`/`healed`/`quarantined`/`failed`/`refused`), `rows_written`, `error` |
| **`run_attempts`** | `id`, `run_key` FK, `attempt` (int), `started_at`, `finished_at`, `state`, `error`, `scope_record_sha256`. **New (R5/M13)** |
| **`resolutions`** | `id`, `run_key` FK, `target`, `field`, `winning_rung` (nullable — null means no rung resolved), `attempts` (JSONB, one entry per rung tried), `node_id`, `ms`, `at`. **New (R5/C4)** |
| `heal_events` | `id`, `run_key` FK, `resolution_id` FK, `target`, `field`, `broke_at`, `winning_rung`, `confirmer_rung`, `confirmer_family`, `selector_before`, `selector_after`, `anchor_before` (JSONB), `anchor_after` (JSONB), `trace` (JSONB), `verdicts` (JSONB), `evidence_uri`, `replayed_ok` (nullable bool), `promoted_by`, `promoted_at` |
| `selector_cache` | `target`, `field`, **`spec_version`** (composite PK), `selector`, `anchor` (JSONB), `node_id`, `set_by_rung`, `set_at`, `set_by_run_key` |
| `quarantine` | `run_key` FK, `reason`, `verdicts` (JSONB), `data_uri`, `resolved_as` (`promoted`/`discarded`/null), `actor`, `resolved_at` |
| `audit_log` | `id`, `at`, `actor`, `action`, `subject`, `detail` (JSONB) |
| `scope_records` | mirror of `ScopeRecord` fields plus `record_sha256`, `loaded_at` |
| **`deploys`** | `target`, `deployed_at`, `source` (`self-host`/`gh-actions`/`manual`), `ref`, `ingested_at`. **New (R17/M10)** — the control arm's ground truth |
| **`interventions`** | `id`, `at`, `actor`, `kind` (`spec_edit`/`cache_edit`/`manual_promote`), `target`, `field`, `before` (JSONB), `after` (JSONB), `reason`. **New (R17/M1)** |

**Four tables were added here rather than later, and the reason is the rule this task already
states.** *"None of them may add a column afterwards, because you cannot compare day 1 to day 90
across a schema migration."* That cuts both ways: a table missing on day one is missing for the whole
log.

- **`resolutions` (C4).** `rung_stats()` is promised in Task 6, required as a *published* claim in
  Task 26 Step 6, and asserted in Task 41 — and `heal_events` only records runs where a heal
  happened. Rung-1 wins were recorded nowhere, so `rung1 82%` was not computable from any table in
  the plan. B11's headline (*"0.0% of resolutions required a model call"*) needs a denominator, and
  this is it.
- **`run_attempts` (M13).** `run_key` is deterministic by design, so a retry after a failure
  overwrites the failed row and the published *"99.2% run success"* is measured on a table that
  silently discards failures. `runs` keeps the terminal state; `run_attempts` keeps the history.
- **`deploys` (M10).** Design §8.1's control-arm claim is *"heals fired only on runs following an
  actual deploy, **verified against deploy history**"*. Unverifiable without a stored feed.
- **`interventions` (M1).** *"Zero manual selector fixes"* is only a claim if manual fixes are
  recorded. Without this table the flagship number has exactly the epistemic status of the vendor
  numbers `00` was written to reject.

**Two key changes, same reasoning:**

- `selector_cache` PK gains `spec_version` (M14). Without it, editing a `FieldTarget.description` —
  i.e. changing what the field *means* — leaves the next run taking a rung-1 cache hit on a selector
  resolved for the old meaning, with the old anchor verifying happily.
- `heal_events.resolution_id` FK and `node_id` on both `resolutions` and `selector_cache`, so a heal
  is joinable to the resolution that produced it and node identity survives into the cache (C5).

**Indexes, also frozen now (M15/P3):** `runs(first_started_at)`, `run_attempts(run_key)`,
`resolutions(run_key)`, `resolutions(target, field, at)`, `heal_events(run_key)`,
`heal_events(target, broke_at)`, `deploys(target, deployed_at)`.

#### Schema additions for Task 3

**Four tables join the frozen day-one schema, and two columns join the `scope_records` mirror.**
Task 3 has not been implemented yet, so adding them now costs nothing, and the freeze rule cuts the
other way for one of them: a table missing on day one is missing for ninety days.

| Table | Columns | Why on day one |
|---|---|---|
| **`operators`** | `id` (PK), `username` (UNIQUE, text), `password_hash` (text), `created_at`, `disabled_at` (nullable) | API spec §3 (closes H3). Holds no log data; added now because it is free |
| **`sessions`** | `token_sha256` (PK, char(64)), `operator_id` (FK `operators.id`), `created_at`, `expires_at`, `revoked_at` (nullable) | API spec §3. **The SHA-256 of the cookie, never the cookie**, so a database read does not yield a usable session |
| **`heartbeats`** | `id` (PK), `target` (text), `scheduled_for` (timestamptz), `fired_at` (timestamptz), `run_key` (text, nullable, **no FK** — a heartbeat is written before any `runs` row exists, and a fire whose spec did not load has no run key at all). Index **`ix_heartbeats_target_scheduled_for` on `(target, scheduled_for)`** | API spec §6.1. **This one is log data**: it is the denominator of the published missed-run count. Task 6's `heartbeat()` "writes a row every scheduled fire" into a table the first draft never named |
| **`findings`** | `id` (PK, text — `Finding.id`), `run_key` (FK `runs.run_key`), `severity` (text), `rule` (text — `properties["rule"]`), `payload` (JSONB — the whole `Finding`, `model_dump(mode="json")`), `at` (timestamptz). Index `ix_findings_run_key` | **Found 2026-09-26, not in the API spec.** Task 29's `evaluate()` returns `list[Finding]` and nothing stores them, so `GET /quality` and `RunDetailView.finding_count` would have no column behind them — a breach of API spec §1 rule 1. Flagged for sign-off with the spec |

`scope_records` (the `ScopeRecord` mirror) gains **`credential_posture` (text, not null, default `'session_injection'` — the field arrives in Task 32, the column now, because the schema freezes on day one)**, **`warmup_runs` (int, not null)** and
**`evidence_retention_days` (int, nullable)**, matching the two `ScopeRecord` fields added to Task 2
below. The mirror stores `origins` and `rate_limit` as JSONB (`rate_limit` as
`{"requests": int, "per_seconds": int}`) and `basis`, `first_heal_policy` as their enum string values.

**Model class names later tasks rely on — declare exactly these in `selector_drift/db/models.py`:**
`Run`, `RunAttempt`, `Resolution`, `HealEvent`, `SelectorCacheEntry`, `Quarantine` (PK `run_key`),
`AuditLog`, `ScopeRecordRow`, `Deploy`, `Intervention`, `Operator`, `OperatorSession` (table
`sessions` — not `Session`, which is `db.session.Session`, the sessionmaker), `Heartbeat`, `Finding`
is **not** used as a class name (it collides with `bok_core.findings.Finding`) — the model is
`FindingRow` (table `findings`).

### Task 4: The browser driver that cannot be handed a bare URL

**Files:**
- Create: `selector_drift/browser/driver.py`, `selector_drift/browser/registry.py`, `selector_drift/browser/limits.py`, `selector_drift/browser/allowlist.py`, `selector_drift/browser/ratelimit.py`
- Modify: `docker-compose.yml` (add the `worker` service)
- Test: `tests/browser/test_driver.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `AuthorisedTarget` (Task 2).
- Produces:
  - `open(target: AuthorisedTarget, credentials: Credentials | None = None) -> Session` — async context manager
  - `Session.page: PageHandle`, `PageHandle.url: str`, `PageHandle.content() -> str`, `PageHandle.screenshot() -> bytes`
  - `registry.url_for(target: str) -> str` — the only place a URL string lives
  - `allowlist.install(context, target) -> None` — **R8/H2.** A Playwright route handler that aborts
    every request whose origin is not in `target.origins`. The scope gate's guarantee is *"no path to
    a page without a scope record"*; that is true of the first navigation and of nothing after it. A
    redirect, an SSO hop, a link click in a nav step or an absolute URL in a spec walks straight off
    the authorised target while still inside an `AuthorisedTarget` context.
  - `ratelimit.acquire(target) -> None` — **R8/H4.** A **persistent** token bucket keyed by target,
    backed by the `audit_log`/Postgres rather than by process memory. The brief requires the limit in
    the scope record (§3.1), the brief's test list names *"rate limit enforced"* (§11), and design
    §4.3 says it is read from the `AuthorisedTarget` and *"is not a tunable"* — and until this
    revision it existed only as the phrase *"applies `target.rate_limit`"* with no step and no test.
    Per-run buckets are not enough: `1 req / 30 s` inside a run says nothing about ten runs starting
    at once.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**

```python
# tests/browser/test_driver.py
import inspect, pytest
from selector_drift import browser

def test_no_public_function_accepts_a_bare_url():
    """Weak by construction -- it only catches a parameter *named* `url` (M19). Kept as a
    typo guard; the real control is test_navigation_off_the_authorised_origin_is_aborted."""
    for name, fn in inspect.getmembers(browser.driver, inspect.isfunction):
        if name.startswith("_"):
            continue
        hints = inspect.get_annotations(fn, eval_str=True)
        assert str not in {hints.get(k) for k in ("url", "href", "path", "target_url")}, name

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_open_loads_a_page(authorised_testbench):
    async with browser.driver.open(authorised_testbench) as session:
        assert "<html" in (await session.page.content()).lower()

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_navigation_off_the_authorised_origin_is_aborted(authorised_testbench, evil_redirect):
    """R8/H2. This is the test the scope gate is *claimed* to have. Without it the gate
    authorises the first navigation and nothing after it."""
    async with browser.driver.open(authorised_testbench) as session:
        with pytest.raises(browser.OffScopeNavigation):
            await session.page.click("#leaves-the-portal")

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_a_subresource_from_another_origin_is_aborted(authorised_testbench):
    async with browser.driver.open(authorised_testbench) as session:
        await session.page.goto_step({"step": "goto", "path": "/results"})
        assert all(r.startswith(tuple(authorised_testbench.origins))
                   for r in session.requested_urls)

def test_the_rate_limit_comes_from_the_target_and_not_from_config(authorised_testbench, monkeypatch):
    """H4, design 4.3: raising it means editing the scope record, which is the document
    you would point at if anyone ever asked why you accessed a system."""
    monkeypatch.setenv("SD_RATE_LIMIT_PER_SECONDS", "0")
    assert ratelimit.window_for(authorised_testbench) == 30

def test_the_limiter_is_persistent_across_processes(authorised_testbench):
    """Ten runs starting at once must not each get their own fresh bucket."""
    ratelimit.acquire(authorised_testbench)
    t0 = time.monotonic(); ratelimit.acquire(authorised_testbench, _fresh_process=True)
    assert time.monotonic() - t0 >= 29
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement the driver**

`open()` reads the URL via `registry.url_for(target.target)`, applies `target.rate_limit` (the limit comes from the `AuthorisedTarget`, never from config), sets the user agent to include `target.user_agent_contact`, launches **one browser context per run**, and tears it down in `__aexit__`.

`limits.py` holds the container limits applied at the Prefect deployment level in Task 6.

- [ ] **Step 4: Add the worker service to compose**

```yaml
  worker:
    build: .
    read_only: true
    user: "10001:10001"
    cap_drop: [ ALL ]
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
      - seccomp=./docker/chromium-seccomp.json   # NOT unconfined -- see below
    tmpfs: [ "/tmp", "/home/app/.cache" ]
    shm_size: 1g              # Chromium's default /dev/shm in Docker is 64 MB
    mem_limit: 2g
    pids_limit: 512
    environment:
      PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH: /opt/pw-browsers   # baked at build, readable by uid 10001
    depends_on: [ postgres, prefect-server ]
```

**The first draft of this block read `security_opt: [ "seccomp=unconfined" ]` (H1).** `00` §8 and
design §9.2 both require *"seccomp default"*; `unconfined` **removes** the filter — the opposite of
the requirement — on the one container in the system that renders hostile HTML while holding session
credentials. It is there because Chromium's own sandbox needs privileges the default profile denies.
Pick one deliberately and write down which:

| Option | Trade |
|---|---|
| Chromium seccomp profile (above) | Keeps a filter. One vendored JSON file to review and pin |
| `--no-sandbox` under `cap_drop: [ALL]` + `no-new-privileges` | Simpler; leans entirely on the container boundary. Acceptable **only** because the container is single-purpose and network-restricted by the allowlist |

`shm_size`, `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` and the writable cache tmpfs are the three things that make
`read_only: true` plus a non-root uid actually boot (B8); the image installs browsers as root and the
service runs as `10001:10001`.

### Task 5: Three scope records and a one-field task spec per target

**Blocked on P-2 and P-3 until they resolve.** Every scope record carries values only a person can
supply — a contact URL that resolves (P-2), two self-owned control-arm hosts (P-3), the bench host
(P-4) and the day-one date. They are written below as `<UPPER-CASE>` tokens, and
`test_no_scope_record_carries_an_unresolved_placeholder` is red until every one is replaced. That is
deliberate: a scope record with an invented date or a 404 contact is a compliance claim that fails
the first time anyone checks it (B4, B5).

**Files:**
- Create: `selector_drift/config.py` — the minimal settings module. **Task 33 extends it** (Step 3
  there replaces this file with its superset; the seven names here keep their meaning)
- Create: `selector_drift/spec/schema.py`, `selector_drift/spec/loader.py`
- Create: `scopes/testbench.yaml`, `scopes/agent-perimeter.yaml`, `scopes/ledger-sense.yaml`
- Create: `specs/testbench.yaml`, `specs/agent-perimeter.yaml`, `specs/ledger-sense.yaml`
- Modify: `.env.example`, `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock` (dev dependency `types-PyYAML`)
- Test: `tests/test_config.py`, `tests/spec/test_spec_schema.py`, `tests/spec/test_loader.py`,
  `tests/scope/test_records_load.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `ScopeRecord`, `Basis`, `FirstHealPolicy` (`selector_drift.scope.record`),
  `authorise(record, *, today)` (`selector_drift.scope.gate`), `ScopeRefusal(reason: str)` with
  `.reason` (`selector_drift.scope.errors`) — all Task 2.
- Produces:
  - `selector_drift/config.py`: `Settings` (frozen dataclass) with fields `env: str` (`SD_ENV`),
    `database_url: str` (`SD_DATABASE_URL`), `spec_dir: Path` (`SD_SPEC_DIR`, default `specs`),
    `scope_dir: Path` (`SD_SCOPE_DIR`, default `scopes`), `evidence_root: Path`
    (`SD_EVIDENCE_ROOT`), `lake_root: Path` (`SD_LAKE_ROOT`), and the property
    `redaction_key -> bytes` (`SD_REDACTION_KEY`, hex, ≥ 32 bytes, raises `ConfigError` when unset —
    no secret has a default); `get_settings() -> Settings` (`lru_cache`d — tests call
    `get_settings.cache_clear()` after changing the environment); `ConfigError(RuntimeError)`
  - `selector_drift/spec/schema.py`:
    - `SpecError(ValueError)`
    - `Relation` — `StrEnum`: `RIGHT_OF = "right_of"`, `BELOW = "below"`, `WITHIN = "within"`
    - `FieldType` — `StrEnum`: `STRING = "string"`, `INTEGER = "integer"`, `DECIMAL = "decimal"`, `DATE = "date"`
    - `DomainRule` — `TypedDict(total=False)`: `min: float`, `max: float`, `enum: list[str]`,
      `date_after: str`, `date_before: str` (ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`); unknown keys refused
    - `AssertionSpec(type: Literal["format", "domain", "cross_field"], pattern: str | None = None, rule: DomainRule | None = None, expression: str | None = None)` — exactly the payload its `type` names
    - `FieldTarget(name: str, description: str, relation: Relation | None = None, assertions: list[AssertionSpec], distributional: bool = False)` — `description` is the semantic target in plain language, never a DOM path
    - `NavStep(step: Literal["goto", "fill", "click"], path: str | None = None, field: str | None = None, value_from: Literal["credentials.username", "credentials.password"] | None = None, role: str | None = None, name: str | None = None)` — exactly as Task 26A Step 3 pins it, validated per step kind
    - `TaskSpec(version: int, scope_ref: str, schedule: str, row_scope: str, natural_key: list[str], expected_schema: dict[str, FieldType], navigate: list[NavStep], targets: list[FieldTarget])`
    - `MAX_MATCH_LENGTH: int = 512`
    - `matches(target: FieldTarget, value: str) -> bool` — **the format matcher lives here, in
      `spec/` (R13/M23).** Task 17's rung 1 must check format assertions and Task 1's contract
      forbids `resolve` → `validate`, so the matcher cannot live in `validate/assertions/format.py`.
      Both packages import it from `spec/`.
  - `selector_drift/spec/loader.py` — **`yaml.safe_load` only** (R13/H5):
    - `load_spec_text(text: str) -> TaskSpec` — raises `yaml.YAMLError` for a YAML tag that would construct an object, `SpecError` for anything else
    - `load_spec(path: Path) -> TaskSpec` — loads exactly `path`; raises `SpecError` (message names the file)
    - `load_scope_text(text: str) -> ScopeRecord`, `load_scope(path: Path) -> ScopeRecord` — raise **`ScopeRefusal`**, never a parse error: a missing, malformed or out-of-enum scope record is a refusal (design §9.3)
    - `spec_file(spec_path: str | Path) -> Path` — an absolute path as given; otherwise `get_settings().spec_dir / name`
    - `scope_file(scope_ref: str) -> Path` — `get_settings().scope_dir / name`
    - `target_of(spec_path: str | Path) -> str` — the file stem; spec files are named `<target>.yaml`

**Why `config.py` is created here and not in Task 33.** Task 33 was the first task to write
`config.py`, but Task 26A's bench fixtures, Task 34B's `derive` fixture and this task's loader all
need `SD_SCOPE_DIR` / `SD_SPEC_DIR` honoured, and the loader is the first code that reads a
directory. The minimal module holds only the seven names the rest of the plan already uses, in the
shape Task 33 gives them (`redaction_key` is a property over the hex string, so a missing key is an
error at use, never a silent default). Task 3's `db/session.py` predates this module and keeps
reading `SD_DATABASE_URL` itself; both must use the same default.

**Three fields added over the first draft, each because something downstream needs them and has no
other source:**

| Field | Needed by | Audit |
|---|---|---|
| `natural_key: list[str]` | Task 28's *"upsert on the natural key"*, Task 30's changeset diff, and `RowKeyContinuity` (Task 22). The phrase "natural key" appeared in the plan with no field anywhere defining one | M5 |
| `row_scope: str` | The cascade resolves per field; a results table is N rows × M fields. Nothing said how per-field resolutions align into rows. `row_scope` names the repeating container ("each row of the results table"), and fields resolve *within* it | M5 |
| `expected_schema` | Task 29 tests `schema_drift` against a baseline that did not exist. Brief §4 lists *"expected schema"* as part of a task spec | M4 |

`FieldTarget.distributional` opts a field into `DistributionalAssertion` (Task 23). It defaults to
`False` because PSI over a high-cardinality identifier column is noise, and *"which fields get a
distributional check at all"* was unspecified (M16).

**Every model forbids unknown keys.** A misspelt `asertions:` that loaded silently would drop a
field's checks without a trace — the green tick `00` §7 calls a lie. The loader refuses it instead.

**The natural key is checked at load, not only by a repo test (M5).** A spec whose `natural_key`
names a column outside `expected_schema`, or a column no target extracts, cannot be deduplicated
(Task 28) and is refused as a `SpecError`. Task 38's `NaturalKeyInSchema` verdict therefore reports
`PASS` for every spec that loads; a violating file is reported by its `SpecSchema` verdict instead.

**A `goto` step takes a same-origin path, never a URL (R8/H2).** The route-handler allowlist
(Task 4) aborts off-origin requests, but a spec that names `https://elsewhere/` is wrong before it
ever reaches a browser, so the schema refuses it.

**A cross-field `expression` is parsed at load and never evaluated here (R13/H5).**
`ast.parse(..., mode="eval")` rejects garbage early; the restricted evaluator that decides what the
expression may *do* is Task 21's `safe_eval`. `spec/` must not import `validate/` — `resolve` imports
`spec`, so `spec → validate` would break the `judged-cannot-call-judge` contract indirectly.

**The control arm's specs name one generic field** — the landing page's main heading — because P-3
has not named the applications. It is honest on day one (the log records run succeeded / failed and
nothing more) and is replaced by a version bump when P-3 resolves; the cache is keyed by
`spec_version` (M14), so the bump cannot reuse a selector resolved for the old meaning.

**Schedules are staggered five minutes apart** (`04:12`, `04:17`, `04:22` UTC). One worker container
with a 2 GB limit runs every extraction (Task 6); three Chromium contexts starting in the same second
is the memory spike B8 warns about, and the persistent rate limiter is per target, not per host.

```python
# tests/spec/test_spec_schema.py
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import pytest
from pydantic import ValidationError

from selector_drift.spec.schema import (MAX_MATCH_LENGTH, AssertionSpec, FieldTarget, NavStep,
                                        Relation, TaskSpec, matches)

CLAIM = FieldTarget(name="claim_number", description="the claim number cell",
                    relation=Relation.RIGHT_OF,
                    assertions=[AssertionSpec(type="format", pattern=r"^[A-Z]{2}\d{8}$")])


def _spec(**overrides: Any) -> TaskSpec:
    base: dict[str, Any] = {
        "version": 1, "scope_ref": "scopes/testbench.yaml", "schedule": "12 4 * * *",
        "row_scope": "each row of the results table", "natural_key": ["claim_number"],
        "expected_schema": {"claim_number": "string"},
        "navigate": [{"step": "goto", "path": "/results"}],
        "targets": [{"name": "claim_number", "description": "the claim number cell",
                     "assertions": [{"type": "format", "pattern": r"^[A-Z]{2}\d{8}$"}]}],
    }
    return TaskSpec.model_validate(base | overrides)


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_a_format_assertion_needs_a_compilable_pattern() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match="does not compile"):
        AssertionSpec(type="format", pattern="([A-Z")


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_an_assertion_carries_exactly_the_payload_its_type_names() -> None:
    """A format assertion with a stray `rule` is a spec author's mistake, not a second check."""
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match="takes exactly `pattern`"):
        AssertionSpec(type="format", pattern="^x$", rule={"min": 1.0})
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match="takes exactly `rule`"):
        AssertionSpec(type="domain")


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_an_unknown_assertion_type_is_refused_at_load() -> None:
    """An unknown type is a refusal, not a skip (00 section 7)."""
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        AssertionSpec.model_validate({"type": "vibes"})


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_a_domain_rule_is_checked_for_sense() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match="min"):
        AssertionSpec(type="domain", rule={"min": 10.0, "max": 1.0})
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match="at least one"):
        AssertionSpec(type="domain", rule={})
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        AssertionSpec(type="domain", rule={"date_after": "01/01/2023"})    # not ISO
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        AssertionSpec.model_validate({"type": "domain", "rule": {"between": [1, 2]}})


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_a_cross_field_expression_must_parse_and_is_never_evaluated_here() -> None:
    """R13/H5. Parsing proves it is an expression; Task 21's safe_eval decides what it may do."""
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match="does not parse"):
        AssertionSpec(type="cross_field", expression="net + ")
    ok = AssertionSpec(type="cross_field", expression="net + tax == gross")
    assert ok.expression == "net + tax == gross"


@pytest.mark.unit
@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", ["https://evil.example/x", "//evil.example/x", "login"])
def test_a_goto_step_takes_a_same_origin_path_never_a_url(path: str) -> None:
    """R8/H2. An absolute URL in a spec walks off the authorised target."""
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match="never a URL"):
        NavStep(step="goto", path=path)


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_each_step_kind_takes_exactly_its_own_keys() -> None:
    assert NavStep(step="goto", path="/").path == "/"
    assert NavStep(step="fill", field="username", value_from="credentials.username").field
    assert NavStep(step="click", role="button", name="Sign in").name == "Sign in"
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        NavStep(step="fill", field="username")                         # no value_from
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        NavStep(step="click", role="button", name="Go", path="/x")     # stray path
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        NavStep(step="fill", field="input[name=user]", value_from="credentials.username")
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        NavStep.model_validate({"step": "fill", "field": "pw", "value_from": "env.PASSWORD"})


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_a_description_with_selector_syntax_is_refused() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match="in words"):
        FieldTarget(name="x", description="table#results > td[2]", assertions=[])


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_unknown_keys_are_refused_not_ignored() -> None:
    """A misspelt `asertions` would otherwise load with no checks at all."""
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        FieldTarget.model_validate({"name": "x", "description": "x", "assertions": [],
                                    "asertions": [{"type": "format", "pattern": "^x$"}]})
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        _spec(sensitivity="SYNTHETIC")


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_the_natural_key_must_be_in_the_schema_and_extracted() -> None:
    """M5. Task 28 upserts on it; a key nobody extracts cannot deduplicate anything."""
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match="expected_schema"):

    with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match="names no target"):
        _spec(expected_schema={"claim_number": "string", "policy_id": "string"},
              natural_key=["policy_id"])


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_duplicate_target_names_are_refused() -> None:
    t = {"name": "claim_number", "description": "the claim number cell", "assertions": []}
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match="duplicate"):

@pytest.mark.unit
@pytest.mark.parametrize("ref", ["../scopes/x.yaml", "/etc/scopes/x.yaml", "scopes/x.yml"])
def test_scope_ref_names_a_file_under_scopes(ref: str) -> None:

@pytest.mark.unit

    assert _spec(schedule="12 4 * * *").schedule == "12 4 * * *"

@pytest.mark.unit
def test_matches_checks_every_format_assertion() -> None:
    two = CLAIM.model_copy(update={"assertions": [

    assert matches(CLAIM, "AB12345678") and matches(CLAIM, "  AB12345678 ")

                       assertions=[AssertionSpec(type="format", pattern=r"^(a+)+$")])
```

```python
    monkeypatch.setenv("SD_SCOPE_DIR", str(tmp_path / "sc"))
    get_settings.cache_clear()
    try:
        assert spec_file("specs/testbench.yaml") == tmp_path / "sp" / "testbench.yaml"
        assert spec_file("testbench.yaml") == tmp_path / "sp" / "testbench.yaml"
        assert spec_file(tmp_path / "x.yaml") == tmp_path / "x.yaml"      # absolute: as given
        assert scope_file("scopes/testbench.yaml") == tmp_path / "sc" / "testbench.yaml"
    finally:
        get_settings.cache_clear()


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_no_module_calls_an_unsafe_yaml_loader() -> None:
    """Global constraint: every YAML loader is yaml.safe_load (R13/H5)."""
    offenders = []
    for path in (REPO / "selector_drift").rglob("*.py"):
        for node in ast.walk(ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))):
            if (isinstance(node, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(node.value, ast.Name)
                    and node.value.id == "yaml" and node.attr in UNSAFE_YAML):
                offenders.append(f"{path.relative_to(REPO)}:{node.lineno} yaml.{node.attr}")
    assert not offenders, offenders
```

```python
@pytest.mark.unit
def test_all_three_day_one_targets_authorise() -> None:
    """`today` is pinned to the record's own authorised_on, not to the wall clock (M20):
    a test that compares dt.date.today() to a hardcoded expires_on is green until that
    date and red afterwards for no reason anyone will remember."""
    # PLACEHOLDER -- P-3 replaces the two control-arm names before day one (OQ1).
    names = {"testbench", "agent-perimeter", "ledger-sense"}
    got = {authorise(r, today=r.authorised_on).target for r in map(load_scope, SCOPES)}
    assert got == names


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_every_scope_record_names_at_least_one_https_origin() -> None:
    """H2. The origins are the browser's allowlist; a deployed target is reached over TLS."""
    for p in SCOPES:
        origins = load_scope(p).origins
        assert origins and all(o.startswith("https://") for o in origins), p.name


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_no_scope_record_carries_an_unresolved_placeholder() -> None:
    """B5/P-2/P-3. Brief 3.3 requires the agent to identify itself with a working contact URL;
    a 404 is a compliance claim that fails the first time anyone checks it. The first draft
    checked only for the string USER and so passed with `<real-account>` still in place."""
    for p in SCOPES:
        found = PLACEHOLDER.findall(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        assert not found, f"{p.name}: {found}"


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_only_the_bench_auto_promotes() -> None:
    auto = {load_scope(p).target for p in SCOPES
            if load_scope(p).first_heal_policy == "auto_promote"}
    assert auto == {"testbench"}


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_only_the_bench_warms_up_fast() -> None:
    """M18. Five runs is permitted only because the bench has an answer key."""
    fast = {load_scope(p).target for p in SCOPES if load_scope(p).warmup_runs < 30}
    assert fast == {"testbench"}


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_no_scope_record_is_dated_in_the_future() -> None:
    """B4. authorised_on is the day the record was signed. A past date stays past, so this
    reads the wall clock without becoming a time bomb."""
    today = dt.datetime.now(dt.UTC).date()
    for p in SCOPES:
        assert load_scope(p).authorised_on <= today, p.name


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_no_scope_record_authors_its_own_sensitivity() -> None:
    """R4/H7. Sensitivity is derived from basis; a typo in an authored label publishes a
    client portal."""
    for p in SCOPES:
        assert "sensitivity" not in yaml.safe_load(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")), p.name


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_an_unknown_target_is_refused_by_the_loader(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """Design 4.3: unknown target -> refuse. A missing file is a refusal, not a crash."""
    with pytest.raises(ScopeRefusal, match="unknown target"):
        load_scope(tmp_path / "nobody.yaml")


@pytest.mark.unit
@pytest.mark.parametrize("text", [
    "!!python/object/apply:os.system ['echo pwned']",
    "target: x\nbasis: public-permissive\n",
])
def test_a_malformed_scope_record_is_a_refusal(text: str) -> None:
    """R13/H5 and design 4.2: a YAML object tag and a basis outside the v1 enum both refuse."""
    with pytest.raises(ScopeRefusal):
        load_scope_text(text)
```

```python
# selector_drift/config.py
"""Process settings, from the environment only. No secret has a default.

Created in Task 5 with the names day one needs. Task 33 replaces this file with its superset
(fixture mode, web origin, public base URL, typegen settings); every name here keeps its meaning.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
from dataclasses import dataclass
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path

DEFAULT_DATABASE_URL = "postgresql+psycopg://selector_drift@localhost:5432/selector_drift"
MIN_REDACTION_KEY_BYTES = 32


class ConfigError(RuntimeError):
    pass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Settings:
    env: str                          # SD_ENV: development | production | test
    database_url: str                 # SD_DATABASE_URL -- Task 3's db/session.py reads it too
    spec_dir: Path                    # SD_SPEC_DIR
    scope_dir: Path                   # SD_SCOPE_DIR -- tests point it at a tmp copy
    evidence_root: Path               # SD_EVIDENCE_ROOT
    lake_root: Path                   # SD_LAKE_ROOT
    _redaction_key_hex: str           # SD_REDACTION_KEY -- hex, >= 32 bytes, never committed

    @property
    def redaction_key(self) -> bytes:
        if not self._redaction_key_hex:
            raise ConfigError("SD_REDACTION_KEY is not set; evidence cannot be redacted")
        key = bytes.fromhex(self._redaction_key_hex)
        if len(key) < MIN_REDACTION_KEY_BYTES:
            raise ConfigError(f"SD_REDACTION_KEY must be at least {MIN_REDACTION_KEY_BYTES} bytes")
        return key


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def get_settings() -> Settings:
    e = os.environ.get
    return Settings(
        env=e("SD_ENV", "development"),
        database_url=e("SD_DATABASE_URL", DEFAULT_DATABASE_URL),
        spec_dir=Path(e("SD_SPEC_DIR", "specs")),
        scope_dir=Path(e("SD_SCOPE_DIR", "scopes")),
        evidence_root=Path(e("SD_EVIDENCE_ROOT", "evidence")),
        lake_root=Path(e("SD_LAKE_ROOT", "lake")),
        _redaction_key_hex=e("SD_REDACTION_KEY", ""),
    )
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Write `spec/schema.py`**

```python
# selector_drift/spec/schema.py
"""The task spec: what to extract, described in words. Config, never code (R13/H5).

A spec names each field by its meaning -- "the claim number cell in the results table" -- never
by a DOM path; the cascade (Tasks 13-18) turns a meaning into an element. Every model forbids
unknown keys: a misspelt `asertions:` that loaded silently would drop a field's checks.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import re
from datetime import date
from enum import StrEnum
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import PurePosixPath
from typing import Annotated, Literal, Self, TypedDict

from pydantic import (AfterValidator, BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, field_validator,
                      model_validator, with_config)

MAX_MATCH_LENGTH = 512
"""Longest value `matches()` will test. A spec pattern meeting a page value is untrusted input on
both sides; bounding the input bounds catastrophic backtracking. Task 21's FormatAssertion uses
the same cap."""


class SpecError(ValueError):
    """A task spec that cannot be used as written. Refused, never repaired."""


class Relation(StrEnum):
    RIGHT_OF = "right_of"
    BELOW = "below"
    WITHIN = "within"


class FieldType(StrEnum):
    STRING = "string"
    INTEGER = "integer"
    DECIMAL = "decimal"
    DATE = "date"


def _iso_date(value: str) -> str:
    if date.fromisoformat(value).isoformat() != value:
        raise ValueError(f"{value!r} is not a YYYY-MM-DD date")
    return value


IsoDate = Annotated[str, AfterValidator(_iso_date)]
FieldName = Annotated[str, Field(pattern=r"^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$")]


@with_config(ConfigDict(extra="forbid"))
class DomainRule(TypedDict, total=False):
    min: float
    max: float
    enum: list[str]
    date_after: IsoDate
    date_before: IsoDate


def _check_rule(rule: DomainRule) -> None:
    if not rule:
        raise ValueError("a domain rule needs at least one of min, max, enum, date_after, "
                         "date_before")
    lo, hi = rule.get("min"), rule.get("max")
    if lo is not None and hi is not None and lo > hi:
        raise ValueError(f"domain rule has min {lo} above max {hi}")
    if "enum" in rule and not rule["enum"]:
        raise ValueError("a domain enum lists at least one value")
    after, before = rule.get("date_after"), rule.get("date_before")
    if after is not None and before is not None and after >= before:
        raise ValueError(f"domain rule date_after {after} is not before date_before {before}")


_PAYLOAD: dict[str, str] = {"format": "pattern", "domain": "rule", "cross_field": "expression"}


class AssertionSpec(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True)

    type: Literal["format", "domain", "cross_field"]
    pattern: str | None = None
    rule: DomainRule | None = None
    expression: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=200)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _exactly_its_own_payload(self) -> Self:
        given = {k for k in _PAYLOAD.values() if getattr(self, k) is not None}
        needed = _PAYLOAD[self.type]
        if given != {needed}:
            raise ValueError(f"a {self.type} assertion takes exactly `{needed}`, "
                             f"got {sorted(given) or 'nothing'}")
        if self.pattern is not None:
            try:
                re.compile(self.pattern)
            except re.error as exc:
                raise ValueError(f"pattern does not compile: {exc}") from exc
        if self.rule is not None:
            _check_rule(self.rule)
        if self.expression is not None:
            try:
                ast.parse(self.expression, mode="eval")       # parsed, NEVER evaluated here
            except SyntaxError as exc:
                raise ValueError(f"cross_field expression does not parse: {exc.msg}") from exc
        return self


_DOM_SYNTAX = re.compile(r"[#\[\]>=]|//|::")


class FieldTarget(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True)

    name: FieldName
    description: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=200)
    relation: Relation | None = None
    assertions: list[AssertionSpec]
    distributional: bool = False

    @field_validator("description")
    @classmethod
    def _words_not_a_selector(cls, value: str) -> str:
        if _DOM_SYNTAX.search(value):
            raise ValueError("describe the field in words; selector syntax (# [ ] > = // ::) "
                             "is a DOM path")
        return value


_NAV_KEYS: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {
    "goto": frozenset({"path"}),
    "fill": frozenset({"field", "value_from"}),
    "click": frozenset({"role", "name"}),
}
_PATH = re.compile(r"^/(?!/)[^\s\\]*$")               # one leading '/', no scheme, no host
_PLAIN_FIELD = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$")    # a form field name, never a selector
_ROLE = re.compile(r"^[a-z]{2,20}$")                   # an ARIA role name


class NavStep(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True)

    step: Literal["goto", "fill", "click"]
    path: str | None = None
    field: str | None = None
    value_from: Literal["credentials.username", "credentials.password"] | None = None
    role: str | None = None
    name: str | None = None

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _exactly_the_keys_its_kind_takes(self) -> Self:
        given = {k for k in ("path", "field", "value_from", "role", "name")
                 if getattr(self, k) is not None}
        wanted = _NAV_KEYS[self.step]
        if given != wanted:
            raise ValueError(f"a {self.step} step takes exactly {sorted(wanted)}, "
                             f"got {sorted(given)}")
        if self.path is not None and not _PATH.fullmatch(self.path):
            raise ValueError("goto takes a same-origin path starting with a single '/', "
                             "never a URL (H2)")
        if self.field is not None and not _PLAIN_FIELD.fullmatch(self.field):
            raise ValueError("fill takes a plain form field name, never a selector")
        if self.role is not None and not _ROLE.fullmatch(self.role):
            raise ValueError("click takes an ARIA role name such as `button`")
        if self.name is not None and not 1 <= len(self.name) <= 80:
            raise ValueError("click takes an accessible name of 1-80 characters")
        return self


_CRON_FIELD = re.compile(r"^[0-9*/,-]+$")


class TaskSpec(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True)

    version: int = Field(ge=1)
    scope_ref: str
    schedule: str
    row_scope: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=200)
    natural_key: list[FieldName] = Field(min_length=1)
    expected_schema: dict[FieldName, FieldType] = Field(min_length=1)
    navigate: list[NavStep]
    targets: list[FieldTarget] = Field(min_length=1)

    @field_validator("scope_ref")
    @classmethod
    def _a_file_under_scopes(cls, value: str) -> str:
        parts = PurePosixPath(value).parts
        if ("\\" in value or len(parts) != 2 or parts[0] != "scopes"
                or not parts[1].endswith(".yaml")):
            raise ValueError("scope_ref is scopes/<target>.yaml")
        return value

    @field_validator("schedule")
    @classmethod
    def _five_field_cron(cls, value: str) -> str:
        fields = value.split()
        if len(fields) != 5 or not all(_CRON_FIELD.fullmatch(f) for f in fields):
            raise ValueError("schedule is a five-field cron expression, evaluated in UTC (M20)")
        return value

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _keys_and_names_agree(self) -> Self:
        names = [t.name for t in self.targets]
        dupes = sorted({n for n in names if names.count(n) > 1})
        if dupes:
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate target names: {dupes}")
        outside = sorted(set(self.natural_key) - set(self.expected_schema))
        if outside:
            raise ValueError(f"natural_key {outside} is not in expected_schema (M5)")
        unextracted = sorted(set(self.natural_key) - set(names))
        if unextracted:
            raise ValueError(f"natural_key {unextracted} names no target: the lake cannot "
                             "deduplicate on a column nobody extracts (M5)")
        return self


@lru_cache(maxsize=256)
def _compiled(pattern: str) -> re.Pattern[str]:
    return re.compile(pattern)


def matches(target: FieldTarget, value: str) -> bool:
    """True when `value` satisfies every format assertion on `target`.

    A value longer than MAX_MATCH_LENGTH never matches. A field with no format assertion has
    nothing to contradict, so it matches; rung 1 then relies on its anchor checks (Task 17).
    """
    text = value.strip()
    if len(text) > MAX_MATCH_LENGTH:
        return False
    return all(_compiled(a.pattern).fullmatch(text) is not None
               for a in target.assertions if a.type == "format" and a.pattern is not None)
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Write `spec/loader.py`**

```python
# selector_drift/spec/loader.py
"""YAML in, typed config out. `yaml.safe_load` and nothing else (R13/H5).

A scope record that is missing, malformed or outside the v1 enum is a refusal, never a crash:
design 9.3 lists "unknown target" and "basis outside the v1 enum" as Refuse, and a refusal is
what the run record and the alert channel report.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import yaml
from pydantic import ValidationError

from selector_drift.config import get_settings
from selector_drift.scope.errors import ScopeRefusal
from selector_drift.scope.record import ScopeRecord
from selector_drift.spec.schema import SpecError, TaskSpec


def load_spec_text(text: str) -> TaskSpec:
    data = yaml.safe_load(text)          # yaml.YAMLError propagates: an object tag is refused here
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise SpecError("a task spec is a YAML mapping")
    try:
        return TaskSpec.model_validate(data)
    except ValidationError as exc:
        raise SpecError(f"invalid task spec: {exc}") from exc


def load_spec(path: Path) -> TaskSpec:
    try:
        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
        raise SpecError(f"no task spec at {path}") from exc
    try:
        return load_spec_text(text)
    except SpecError as exc:
        raise SpecError(f"{path}: {exc}") from exc


def load_scope_text(text: str) -> ScopeRecord:
    try:
        data = yaml.safe_load(text)
    except yaml.YAMLError as exc:
        raise ScopeRefusal(f"scope record is not valid YAML: {exc}") from exc
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise ScopeRefusal("a scope record is a YAML mapping")
    try:
        return ScopeRecord.model_validate(data)
    except ValidationError as exc:
        raise ScopeRefusal(f"invalid scope record: {exc}") from exc


def load_scope(path: Path) -> ScopeRecord:
    try:
        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
        raise ScopeRefusal(f"unknown target: no scope record at {path}") from exc
    try:
        return load_scope_text(text)
    except ScopeRefusal as exc:
        raise ScopeRefusal(f"{path}: {exc.reason}") from exc


def spec_file(spec_path: str | Path) -> Path:
    """An absolute path as given; anything else by file name under SD_SPEC_DIR."""
    p = Path(spec_path)
    return p if p.is_absolute() else get_settings().spec_dir / p.name


def scope_file(scope_ref: str) -> Path:
    """A spec's `scopes/<target>.yaml`, resolved under SD_SCOPE_DIR."""
    return get_settings().scope_dir / Path(scope_ref).name


def target_of(spec_path: str | Path) -> str:
    """Spec files are named `<target>.yaml`; test_loader pins it for every file in specs/."""
    return Path(spec_path).stem
```

**Corrections to the first draft of this task.** Its `test_the_loader_refuses_a_yaml_tag...` used
`pytest`, `yaml` and `load_spec_text` without importing any of them; its placeholder test passed with
`<real-account>` still in the file; its "PASS, 9 tests" counted tests that did not exist; and it

rather than the refusal design §4.3 requires.

### Task 6: The cron fires and writes a run record — the log has started

**Files:**
- Create: `selector_drift/orchestrate/run_record.py`, `selector_drift/orchestrate/flows.py`,
  `selector_drift/orchestrate/deployments.py`, `selector_drift/orchestrate/rung_stats.py`
- Create: `selector_drift/quality/alerts.py` (the one alert channel — Task 29A builds `notify()` on it)
- Create: `selector_drift/__main__.py`
- Create: `Dockerfile`, `.dockerignore`, `docker/postgres-init/10-prefect-database.sql`
- Create: `docs/methodology.md`
- Modify: `docker-compose.yml` (add `prefect-server`; give Task 4's `worker` its command, restart
  policy, init and environment; mount the Postgres init directory), `.env.example`
- Test: `tests/orchestrate/conftest.py`, `tests/orchestrate/test_run_key.py`,
  `tests/orchestrate/test_run_record.py`, `tests/orchestrate/test_rung_stats.py`,
  `tests/orchestrate/test_deployments.py`, `tests/quality/test_alert_channel.py`,
  `tests/test_main.py`, `tests/test_methodology_log_start.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `authorise`, `ScopeRefusal`, `AuthorisedTarget` (Task 2 — `target.record_sha256`,
  `target.target`); `Run`, `RunAttempt`, `Heartbeat`, `Resolution`, `AuditLog`, `Session`, `engine`
  (Task 3); `selector_drift.browser.driver.open(target, credentials=None)` — async context manager
  yielding a session whose `page.content()` returns the HTML — and `selector_drift.browser.registry.url_for`
  (Task 4); `load_spec`, `load_scope`, `spec_file`, `scope_file`, `target_of`, `SpecError`,
  `get_settings` (Task 5).
- Produces — `selector_drift/orchestrate/run_record.py` (**not** `flows.py`: Task 26A's `pipeline.py`
  needs these and `flows.py` imports `pipeline.py`, so keeping them in `flows.py` would make the
  import circular):
  - `run_key(target: str, spec_version: int, window: str) -> str` — deterministic,
    `f"{target}:{spec_version}:{window}"`, `window` an ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`; raises `ValueError` for a
    target that is not `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$` or a window that is not exactly ISO. **Every
    later task uses this exact function for idempotency.**
  - `parse_run_key(key: str) -> tuple[str, int, date]`
  - `window_for(slot: datetime) -> str` — the UTC date of the cron slot, not of the fire (M20);
    refuses a naive datetime
  - `TerminalState = Literal["completed", "healed", "quarantined", "failed", "refused"]` — the frozen five;
    `AttemptState = Literal["started", "completed", "healed", "quarantined", "failed"]`
  - `heartbeat(target: str, scheduled_for: datetime, run_key: str | None, *, fired_at: datetime | None = None) -> int`
    — one `Heartbeat` row per `(target, scheduled_for)`, idempotent (a Prefect retry of the same
    slot returns the existing id rather than counting the fire twice); returns the row id
  - `link_heartbeat(heartbeat_id: int, run_key: str) -> None`
  - `next_attempt(run_key: str) -> int` — `1 + max(attempt)` for the key, so a retry **or a second
    run in the same window** appends an attempt rather than overwriting attempt 1 (M13)
  - `record_attempt(run_key: str, attempt: int, state: AttemptState, error: str | None, scope_record_sha256: str) -> None`
    — upserts one `run_attempts` row on `(run_key, attempt)`; `"started"` also marks the `runs` row
    `failed` with `NO_TERMINAL_STATE` until a terminal state replaces it, so a crash, kill or timeout
    reads as a failure, never as a missing row. **Called only after `authorise()` returns.**
  - `record_run(key: str, *, target: str, spec_version: int, window: date, state: TerminalState, rows_written: int | None = None, error: str | None = None) -> None`
    — the terminal state on `runs`, upserted; `first_started_at` survives
  - `record_authorisation(run_key: str, target: str, record_sha256: str) -> None` — one `audit_log`
    row (`action="scope_authorised"`), the promise Task 2 makes: *"which authorisation was in force
    when we accessed this system"* is answerable from the database
  - `NO_TERMINAL_STATE: str`
- Produces — `selector_drift/orchestrate/flows.py`:
  - `extraction_flow(spec_path: str) -> str` — Prefect flow (`retries=2`, `retry_delay_seconds=300`,
    `timeout_seconds=600`), returns the `run_key`
  - `scheduled_slot() -> datetime` — `prefect.runtime.flow_run.scheduled_start_time` as a UTC
    `datetime` (the cron slot, not the wall clock)
  - `load_start_page(target: AuthorisedTarget) -> int` (async), `StartPageError(RuntimeError)`
- Produces — `selector_drift/orchestrate/rung_stats.py`: `rung_stats() -> dict[str, float]` —
  proportion of resolutions won by each rung, keys `rung1`…`rung5`, **computed from the
  `resolutions` table (R5/C4)**, not from `heal_events`; `{}` until the first resolution (Phase C).
  Its denominator is every resolution attempted, including rung-1 cache hits and resolutions no
  rung won (B11). Task 34B makes it delegate to `derive.rung_shares()`.
- Produces — `selector_drift/orchestrate/deployments.py`: `JOB_LIMITS`,
  `extraction_deployments() -> list[RunnerDeployment]`, `main() -> None` (registers and serves;
  blocks)
- Produces — `selector_drift/quality/alerts.py`: `AlertKind`, `WEBHOOK_ENV = "SD_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL"`,
  `webhook_url() -> str | None`, `post_alert(kind: AlertKind, target: str, run_key: str | None, summary: str) -> bool`
- Produces — `selector_drift/__main__.py`: `main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int` with one
  subcommand, `run <spec>`. Task 34 adds `create-operator`.

**Day one does exactly this, in this order, and nothing else** (design §8 — no cascade exists yet;
Task 26A replaces everything after the authorisation block):

```
heartbeat(stem, slot, None)          FIRST: before the spec loads, before any authorisation (API spec 6.1)
load_spec(spec_file(spec_path))      SpecError -> raise; the heartbeat stays, unlinked (run_key NULL)
key = run_key(stem, version, window_for(slot));  link_heartbeat(beat, key)
load_scope + stem check + authorise  ScopeRefusal -> runs.state=refused, alert, NO run_attempts row
next_attempt; record_attempt(started); record_authorisation
driver.open(target) -> page.content()   any exception -> attempt failed, runs failed, alert, re-raise
record_attempt(completed); record_run(completed)
```

**Why the heartbeat comes before the spec loads (B3, API spec §6.1).** The first amendment loaded
the spec first and wrote the heartbeat afterwards, so a spec that loaded but whose *scope* file was
missing left no heartbeat at all — a fire indistinguishable from a host that was down. The heartbeat
is now the flow's first statement, keyed by the spec file's stem (Task 5 pins stem = target for every
spec), and `link_heartbeat()` attaches the run key once it is known. A refused, crashed or
misconfigured run leaves a heartbeat; a host that was down leaves nothing, which `missed_runs`
(Task 34B) counts as missed — the honest reading (design §9.2).

**Why a refusal writes no `run_attempts` row.** `derive.fired_without_attempt` (Task 34B) tells "the
scope gate refused" from "the scheduler never fired" by exactly that absence. `record_attempt()` is
called only after `authorise()` returns.

**Why the attempt number is `next_attempt(key)`, not `flow_run.run_count` (M13).** `run_count` is 1
for every *new* flow run, so a second run in the same UTC window — a manual re-run, or a late run
after a host restart — would upsert over attempt 1 and erase the failure it retried. Counting the
rows that exist appends instead.

**Why a started attempt marks the run `failed` until it finishes.** `runs.state` holds the frozen
five (API spec §4.3), so there is no "running" state to leave behind. A worker killed by the memory
limit or the 10-minute timeout never reaches its `except` block; with this rule its run reads
`failed: attempt started; no terminal state was recorded`, which is true, instead of the previous
day's `completed`, which is not.

**Why the limits live on the container, and are also declared on the deployment (B8).** The worker
runs `serve()` — a process runner — so Prefect's `job_variables` are not applied by anything on the
VM today. The enforcement is the `worker` service's `mem_limit: 2g` / `pids_limit: 512` (Task 4) and
the flow's `timeout_seconds=600`. `job_variables` carry the same values so a later move to a Docker
work pool keeps them, and `test_the_container_enforces_the_limits_the_deployment_declares` fails if
the two ever disagree — a declared limit nothing enforces is a green tick with no test behind it.

**Why the first alert channel lands on day one (M2).** A refusal or a failed run at 04:12 that
notifies nobody stalls the log silently, and DoD 7 requires *"data-quality contracts **and
alerting**"*. One webhook is enough for v1. Task 29A adds dedup, findings, quarantines and missed
heartbeats on top of `post_alert()`; nothing later has to invent a channel. An unset webhook is
logged loudly at startup and at every alert, because an alerting system nobody configured is worse
than none.

```python
from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as dt
import functools
import socket
import threading
from collections.abc import Iterator
from http.server import SimpleHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import yaml

from sqlalchemy import text

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
PAGE = ("<!doctype html><html><head><title>Day one</title></head>"
```
